paper.title_en: Symmetric entanglers for noninvertible symmetry-protected topological phases
paper.abstract_en: It has been suggested that noninvertible symmetry-protected topological phases (SPT), due to the lack of a stacking structure, do not have symmetric entanglers (globally symmetric finite-depth quantum circuits) connecting them. Using topological holography, we argue that a symmetric entangler should in fact exist for <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow></math> systems whenever the noninvertible symmetry has SPT phases connected by fixed-charge dualities. Moreover, we construct an explicit example of a symmetric entangler for the two SPT phases with <math><mrow><mi>Rep</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> symmetry, as a matrix product unitary.
